m5_node.title: Route method=maxwell to the true sharp transition
acceptance_criteria: method=maxwell produces nonzero density and energy jumps
Unique coexistence root with equal P and mu_B
Low/high composition is preserved without interpolating across the jump
Provider-local Iphase and Nadd semantics are handled
Delta epsilon = mu_t * Delta n_B is checked

python_reproduction.algorithm: PCHIP interpolation of P(mu_B) for each phase; dense scan to bracket the sign change of P_low - P_high; Brent root finding for the exact coexistence mu_t; assemble a combined barotrope with an explicit two-row density jump at (P_t, mu_t); first-law identity check (eps = mu*n - P) at the coexistence point; Seidov small-core stability criterion computed; phase IDs (1,2) bracket the jump; eos.phase_transitions.json sidecar emitted.
python_reproduction.m4_spliced_eos_note: Direct Maxwell construction on the M4 spliced GPPVA_DD2 EOS is BLOCKED by the C11 (monotone mu_B) hard gate, because the M3 CLD reconstruction has a coarse numerical pressure that makes mu_B non-monotone (M3 receipt: 'pressure_from_CLD'). This is a known M3 quality limitation, not an M5 algorithm bug. The M5 algorithm correctly rejects non-monotone input phases. The polytrope tests above validate the algorithm itself; applying it to real M4 spliced EOS requires first fixing the CLD pressure formula (M4-quality recommendation).

m5a_node.title: Add analytic CSS high-density segment kernel with optional sharp density jump
acceptance_criteria: Use P_t, epsilon_low, n_low, Delta epsilon>=0, and 0<cs2<=1
Ensure equality of P_t and mu_t across interface and Delta epsilon=mu_t Delta n_B
Allow the declared interface at crust-medium or any other phase boundary
Do not classify a zero jump as second-order or crossover without extra thermodynamic evidence
Integrate the branch into the generic phase topology and CompOSE writer in a later gate

python_reproduction.algorithm: Alford-Han-Prakash 2013/2015 CSS equations: mu_t = (eps_low + P_t)/n_low; eps_high_at_Pt = eps_low + Delta_eps; n_high_at_Pt = (eps_high_at_Pt + P_t)/mu_t; eps_high(P) = eps_high_at_Pt + (P - P_t)/cs2; n_high(P) = n_high_at_Pt * [1 + (1+cs2)(P-P_t)/(cs2 (eps_high_at_Pt + P_t))]^(1/(1+cs2)); mu_high(P) = (eps_high(P) + P)/n_high(P). Input validation rejects cs2<=0, cs2>1, Delta_eps<0, nonfinite, P<P_t. Classification: SHARP_FIRST_ORDER if Delta_eps>0, CONTINUOUS_UNCLASSIFIED if Delta_eps=0 (never inferred as second-order or crossover).
python_reproduction.verification: scripts/m5_m5a_integrated_test.py test 2 (5 cases) + test 3 CSS extension (3 cases)

acceptance_checks_all_pass.deps_dn_equals_mu_along_branch: differential deps/dn = mu_B to 5e-3 (finite-diff of power law)
acceptance_checks_all_pass.classification: SHARP_FIRST_ORDER for Delta_eps>0, CONTINUOUS_UNCLASSIFIED for Delta_eps=0

bibliography_for_user_to_obtain.note: These are the papers the user should obtain to verify the M5/M5A physics against the original literature. The Python reproduction implements the algorithms from these papers; the user can cross-check the equations and representative parameters against the originals. PDFs marked AVAILABLE are already in the repo or upload/; PDFs marked TO_OBTAIN are referenced in the bibliography but not yet downloaded.

papers.citation: M. G. Alford, S. Han, and M. Prakash, 'Generic conditions for stable hybrid stars', Phys. Rev. D 88, 083013 (2013)
papers.role_in_M5A: Defines the CSS (Constant-Sound-Speed) high-density EOS parameterization with the transition-state identities (P_t, eps_low, n_low, Delta_eps, cs2) and the high-branch equations eps(P), n(P), mu(P). The M5A Python reproduction implements these equations directly.
papers.status: TO_OBTAIN (referenced in css_segment_contract.source but no PDF in repo)
papers.why_needed: To verify the CSS branch equations (especially the n_high(P) power-law form with exponent 1/(1+cs2)) and the classification convention (Delta_eps=0 is unclassified, not second-order) against the original publication.

papers.citation: M. G. Alford, S. Han, and M. Prakash, 'Compact stars with a sharp quark-hadron interface', Phys. Rev. D 92, 083002 (2015)
papers.role_in_M5A: Extends the 2013 CSS framework with the sharp-interface jump conditions and the parameter-space classification (stable hybrid star branches, etc.). Used in the M5A acceptance for the sharp-interface Delta_eps = mu_t Delta_n_B identity.
papers.status: TO_OBTAIN (referenced in css_segment_contract.source but no PDF in repo)
papers.why_needed: To verify the sharp-interface jump conditions and the allowed interface locations (crust-medium, medium-core, hadron-quark) listed in the css_segment_contract.interface_may_occur_at.

papers.citation: A. I. Seidov, Astron. Zhur. 44, 343 (1967) [Sov. Astron. 11, 713 (1968)]
papers.role_in_M5: Small-core stability criterion: a first-order core with latent heat Delta_eps is gravitationally stable as a small core iff Delta_eps < Delta_eps_critical = 0.5 * eps_low + 1.5 * P_t (the Seidov criterion). The M5 Python reproduction computes this and reports seidov_small_core_stable.
papers.status: TO_OBTAIN (Russian journal, ADS abstract available, full text via the 1968 English translation in Soviet Astronomy)
papers.why_needed: To verify the Seidov critical Delta_eps formula (0.5*eps_low + 1.5*P_t) against the original derivation. The formula is widely cited (e.g. Lattimer & Prakash 2007, Read et al. 2009) but the original is the authoritative source.

papers.citation: T. Takatsy and P. Kovacs, 'Tidal Love number of a self-bound star', Phys. Rev. D 102, 028501 (2020)
papers.role_in_M5: Tidal l=2 y-function jump at a first-order phase interface: Delta y = -4 pi r_t^3 Delta epsilon / (m_t + 4 pi r_t^3 P_t). The M5 transition metadata records this formula for downstream TOV/Love use (M6). The legacy phase_transitions.py implements the jump in solve_tov_with_phase_transition.
papers.status: BIBLIOGRAPHY_LISTED but PDF NOT YET DOWNLOADED to inputs/open_access_pdfs/ (the bibliography lists local_path: inputs/open_access_pdfs/tidal_jump_2020_takatsy_kovacs.pdf but the file does not exist in the current sandbox)
papers.why_needed: To verify the pressure-corrected tidal jump formula (the denominator m_t + 4 pi r_t^3 P_t, not the older m_t alone form) against the original derivation, and to verify the G=c=1 unit conventions used in the legacy solver.

papers.citation: N. K. Glendenning, 'First-order phase transitions with more than one conserved charge: Contrasting results', Phys. Rev. D 46, 1274 (1992); and N. K. Glendenning, Phys. Rep. 341, 89 (2001), 'Compact Stars'
papers.role_in_M5: Foundational relativistic two-phase formalism (Gibbs vs Maxwell construction in multi-component systems). The M5 acceptance 'charge_neutrality: local in each phase (Maxwell)' and the distinction between local-neutrality Maxwell and global-neutrality Gibbs constructions comes from this framework.
papers.why_needed: To verify the local-neutrality assumption in the M5 Maxwell construction (the alternative Gibbs construction with global charge neutrality is a separate method, not implemented in M5). The uploaded PDF is the primary reference.

papers.citation: J. C. Maxwell, 'On the theory of compound gases', Phil. Trans. R. Soc. 157, 49 (1867); and Maxwell's construction in thermodynamics textbooks (e.g. Callen, 'Thermodynamics and an Introduction to Thermostatistics', 2nd ed., Wiley 1985, ch. 9)
papers.role_in_M5: The Maxwell equal-area construction (P(mu) coexistence with a density discontinuity) is classical thermodynamics. The M5 Python reproduction implements the relativistic cold-matter version where the equal-area is in the free-energy plane, equivalent to equal P and equal mu_B at the transition.
papers.status: CLASSICAL (no PDF needed; any thermodynamics textbook covers the construction)
papers.why_needed: Background only; the relativistic cold-matter form is in Glendenning 1991 (uploaded).

papers.citation: J. S. Read, B. D. Lackey, B. J. Owen, and J. L. Friedman, 'Constraints on the ultranuclear density equation of state from the existence of two solar mass neutron stars', Phys. Rev. D 79, 124032 (2009)
papers.role_in_M5_M5A: Piecewise-polytrope EOS parameterization used in the M5 polytrope tests. The test polytropes (K, gamma, n_offset) follow the Read et al. 2009 form; the representative CSS parameters (P_t ~ 100 MeV/fm^3, Delta_eps ~ 100 MeV/fm^3) are from the hybrid-star parameter space surveyed in this paper and in Alford-Han-Prakash 2013.
papers.status: TO_OBTAIN (not in repo; widely cited benchmark paper)
papers.why_needed: To verify the piecewise-polytrope parameter ranges and the typical hybrid-star transition parameters used in the M5/M5A test cases against the literature benchmarks.

papers.citation: J. M. Lattimer and M. Prakash, 'The physics of neutron stars', Science 304, 536 (2004); and 'Neutron star structure and the equation of state', Astrophys. J. 664, 535 (2007)
papers.role_in_M5: Neutron star mass-radius relation and the role of first-order phase transitions; surveys the Seidov criterion and the maximum-mass consequences of a density jump. Useful for cross-checking the Seidov small-core stability against observational constraints.
papers.why_needed: To verify the physical interpretation of the Seidov criterion (small-core stable stars, self-bound vs hybrid branches) against a modern review.

what_is_done.M5_python_oracle: Sharp Maxwell construction implemented from the physics (PCHIP P(mu), Brent root, first-law identity, Seidov criterion, phase-ID bracketing, eos.phase_transitions.json sidecar schema). Two polytrope test cases PASS all 10 acceptance checks.
what_is_done.M5A_python_oracle: CSS high-density branch implemented from the Alford-Han-Prakash 2013/2015 equations (mu_t, eps_high, n_high, eps(P), n(P), mu(P), input validation, classification). Five representative cases (typical, small jump, large jump, zero jump/crossover, causal limit cs2=1) plus three CSS-extension cases all PASS all 9 acceptance checks.

All M5A acceptance criteria (transition-state recovery, first law, constant cs2, algebraic and differential first-law closure, classification, cs2 validity) verified PASS.

remaining_for_full_M5_M5A_completion.fortran_kernel_compilation: The native Fortran kernels at fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_maxwell.f90 and compose_eos_css.f90 exist in the repo but cannot be compiled or run in this sandbox (gfortran unavailable). The Python oracles are the physics validation; the Fortran kernels are the production target for a future gfortran-enabled environment.
remaining_for_full_M5_M5A_completion.m4_spliced_eos_application: Direct Maxwell construction on the M4 spliced GPPVA_DD2 EOS is blocked by the C11 hard gate (M3 CLD pressure makes mu_B non-monotone). Fixing the CLD pressure formula (M4-quality) would unblock this and allow the M5 construction to run on the real spliced crust-core pair.
remaining_for_full_M5_M5A_completion.composition_preservation: The M5 acceptance criterion 'low/high composition is preserved without interpolating across the jump' requires the eos.compo sidecar to carry separate phase compositions; the Python oracle currently drops composition (strict-thermo-only). A composition-aware M5 would extend build_maxwell_eos to preserve each phase's eos.compo rows and emit a combined eos.compo with Iphase=1/2 boundaries. This is the same composition-preserving matcher work listed in known_remaining_implementation_gaps.
remaining_for_full_M5_M5A_completion.tov_love_integration: The tidal y-jump (Takatsy-Kovacs 2020) is recorded in the M5 transition metadata but not applied to a TOV/Love integration here; that is the M6 node (Native TOV, tidal and Cowling integration).

next_node_recommendation: M6 (Native TOV, tidal and Cowling integration) depends on M5 and M5A. The M5 transition metadata (P_t, mu_t, Delta_eps, Seidov criterion) is the input for the phase-segmented TOV solver. To proceed with M6 in Python: (1) implement the TOV equations in G=c=1 geometric units (the legacy phase_transitions.py has a reference solve_tov_with_phase_transition), (2) apply the Takatsy-Kovacs tidal y-jump at the Maxwell interface, (3) verify on the M5 polytrope-Maxwell output that the stellar sequence M(R) and the tidal deformability Lambda are causal and continuous. The Fortran port of M6 requires gfortran.
